test_cases.title: Subscribe to All Data-of-Interest Bus Messages
test_cases.setup: Initialize mlog_app under POSIX with a mocked software bus that records every Subscribe() call by message ID.
procedure: Invoke mlog_app initialization entry point.
Capture the set of message IDs subscribed via the mocked bus.
Compare the captured set against the configured data-of-interest manifest.
test_cases.acceptance_criteria: Captured subscription set equals the data-of-interest manifest; no required ID is missing and no extra IDs are present.

test_cases.title: Forward Each Subscribed Message Without Downsampling
test_cases.setup: Initialize mlog_app with a fake mlog_lib that counts records by source ID. Inject 100 IMU and 50 baro messages on the mocked bus.
procedure: Publish 100 distinct IMU messages onto the mocked bus.
Publish 50 distinct baro messages onto the mocked bus.
Drive mlog_app to process all queued messages.
Read the per-source forwarded record counts from the fake mlog_lib.
test_cases.acceptance_criteria: Fake mlog_lib reports exactly 100 forwarded IMU records and exactly 50 forwarded baro records, in the order produced.

test_cases.title: Initiate New Log Run on Startup
test_cases.setup: Initialize mlog_app with a fake mlog_lib that records each NewRun() invocation with arguments and call ordering.
procedure: Invoke mlog_app initialization entry point.
Inspect the fake mlog_lib invocation log.
Verify NewRun() was invoked before any record-forwarding call.
test_cases.acceptance_criteria: Fake mlog_lib records exactly one NewRun() call during init, occurring strictly before any forwarded record call.

test_cases.title: Preserve Prior Log Runs Across Startups
test_cases.setup: Stage a fake filesystem root containing two prior run directories (run_0001, run_0002) with sentinel files. Wire mlog_app to a real mlog_lib backed by the staged root.
procedure: Snapshot the staged root contents (paths and sentinel hashes).
Initialize mlog_app, triggering a new run.
Re-snapshot the staged root contents.
Diff the prior run directory contents between the two snapshots.
test_cases.acceptance_criteria: All prior run directories and sentinel files exist with identical content after startup; no prior run is deleted, truncated, or overwritten.

test_cases.title: Stamp Forwarded Records With Monotonic Microseconds
test_cases.setup: Initialize mlog_app with a fake monotonic clock and a fake mlog_lib capturing record timestamps.
procedure: Set the fake clock to t0 = 1000 us and publish a bus message; advance the fake clock to t1 = 2500 us and publish another.
Advance the clock to t2 = 9000 us and publish a third bus message.
Drive mlog_app to process the queued messages.
Read the captured timestamps from the fake mlog_lib.
test_cases.acceptance_criteria: Captured timestamps equal {1000, 2500, 9000} microseconds (monotonic, non-decreasing, in microsecond units).

test_cases.title: Per-Sample Timestamp Present on Every Record
test_cases.setup: Initialize mlog_app with a fake mlog_lib that captures every forwarded record header.
procedure: Publish a mixed sequence of 200 sensor messages (IMU, baro, magnetometer) onto the mocked bus.
Drive mlog_app to process all messages.
Inspect each captured record header for the timestamp field.
test_cases.acceptance_criteria: Every one of the 200 forwarded records carries a populated timestamp field; no record has an absent or default-zero timestamp.

test_cases.title: Forward NMEA Sentences Verbatim
test_cases.setup: Initialize mlog_app with a fake mlog_lib that captures the byte payload of each forwarded NMEA record.
procedure: Publish a known NMEA GGA sentence (including leading $ and trailing CR/LF) onto the bus.
Publish a known NMEA RMC sentence with checksum onto the bus.
Drive mlog_app to process both messages.
Compare each captured payload to the input sentence byte-for-byte.
test_cases.acceptance_criteria: Each forwarded NMEA payload byte sequence is bit-identical to the input sentence (including framing and checksum bytes).

test_cases.title: Forward GPS UTC Records to Library
test_cases.setup: Initialize mlog_app with a fake mlog_lib that counts and captures forwarded GPS UTC records.
procedure: Publish three distinct GPS UTC messages with different UTC values onto the bus.
Drive mlog_app to process all queued messages.
Read the captured GPS UTC records from the fake mlog_lib.
test_cases.acceptance_criteria: Fake mlog_lib captured exactly three GPS UTC records, in publish order, with UTC fields equal to the input values.

test_cases.title: Continue Forwarding After SD Write Failure
test_cases.setup: Initialize mlog_app with a fake mlog_lib whose write call returns a write-failure status on call N=5 and success otherwise.
procedure: Publish 10 sequential bus messages onto the mocked bus.
Drive mlog_app to process all 10 messages.
Verify mlog_app did not abort or exit on the failure.
Count the number of forwarding attempts observed by the fake mlog_lib.
test_cases.acceptance_criteria: mlog_app attempts all 10 forwards (including calls 6 through 10 after the failure on call 5); mlog_app remains in the running state.

test_cases.title: Publish SD Card Health Status Reflects Recent Outcomes
test_cases.setup: Initialize mlog_app with a fake mlog_lib whose write outcomes are scriptable and a mocked bus that captures every published SD health message.
procedure: Script the fake mlog_lib to return success for 5 writes; publish 5 bus messages and process them.
Capture the latest SD health message published by mlog_app.
Script the fake mlog_lib to return write failure for the next 3 writes; publish 3 bus messages and process them.
Capture the latest SD health message published by mlog_app.
test_cases.acceptance_criteria: After the success batch, the published SD health status indicates a healthy state; after the failure batch, the published SD health status indicates a degraded or failed state.

test_cases.title: POSIX and Pico2 Builds Produce Equivalent Forwarding Behavior
test_cases.setup: Build mlog_app for both POSIX and Pico2 targets. Provide an identical scripted bus message sequence and identical fake mlog_lib backend on both targets that captures forwarded records to a normalized text trace.
procedure: Run the scripted message sequence against the POSIX build and capture the normalized trace.
Run the same scripted sequence against the Pico2 build (host-loop or HIL) and capture the normalized trace.
Diff the two normalized traces (record source, payload, sequence ordering).
test_cases.acceptance_criteria: POSIX trace and Pico2 trace are byte-identical with respect to forwarded record source ID, payload bytes, and ordering.

test_cases.title: Deterministic Forwarding for Identical Input Sequences
test_cases.setup: Initialize mlog_app with a fake mlog_lib capturing forwarded records and a fake monotonic clock driven from a fixed script.
procedure: Run a fixed scripted bus message sequence end-to-end and capture the trace of forwarded records (run A).
Reset mlog_app and the fakes to their initial state.
Run the identical scripted sequence end-to-end and capture the trace (run B).
Diff trace A against trace B.
test_cases.acceptance_criteria: Trace A and trace B are byte-identical: same record count, same source IDs, same payload bytes, same timestamps, same ordering.

test_cases.title: No Forwarding Before NewRun Initialization
test_cases.setup: Initialize mlog_app with a fake mlog_lib that timestamps each call and a mocked bus with a pre-loaded message published before init completes.
procedure: Pre-publish one bus message onto the mocked bus prior to invoking mlog_app init.
Invoke mlog_app initialization, then drive one process tick.
Inspect the fake mlog_lib call log ordering.
test_cases.acceptance_criteria: The first recorded mlog_lib call is NewRun(); any forwarded record calls occur strictly after NewRun() in the call log.

test_cases.title: Timestamp Monotonicity Across Mixed Sources
test_cases.setup: Initialize mlog_app with a fake monotonic clock and a fake mlog_lib capturing per-record timestamps and source IDs.
procedure: Interleave 50 IMU, 25 baro, and 25 GPS UTC messages onto the bus, advancing the fake clock by 100 us before each publish.
Drive mlog_app to process the queued messages.
Extract the captured timestamp sequence in forward order.
test_cases.acceptance_criteria: Captured timestamps are strictly non-decreasing across all 100 records regardless of source, with each adjacent pair differing by at least 100 us.
